subject: physics_2
question_text: Distinguish between transverse and longitudinal waves.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: in a transverse wave the particle vibration is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation (string waves, light); in a longitudinal wave it is parallel (sound in air). In both types the particles only vibrate about their mean positions — neither wave carries the particles along.

recall_prompt: Say the difference between the two wave types — the direction of vibration in each, with one example each.

steps.label: Transverse waves
lines: In a transverse wave, each particle of the
direction in which the wave travels.
Example: waves on a stretched string.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word perpendicular is the mark; the example makes the answer safe.
steps.why: The two wave types differ in one thing only — the angle between the particle vibration and the wave direction — so the definition must name that angle.
common_mistakes: Saying the particles travel with the wave. In both wave types each particle only vibrates about its mean position.
Writing perpendicular without saying perpendicular to WHAT — it is the direction of wave propagation.

recall.must_convey: That in a transverse wave the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction the wave travels.
accept: particles vibrate perpendicular to the wave direction
vibration is at right angles to propagation
reject: particles vibrate parallel to the wave direction

steps.memory_tip: Transverse — across. The particle moves across the line the wave travels on.

steps.label: Longitudinal waves
lines: In a longitudinal wave, each particle
vibrates parallel to the direction in
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Parallel is the mark word; sound in air is the standard example.
steps.why: Parallel vibration is what lets a longitudinal wave travel as compressions and rarefactions — the particles push together and spread apart along the same line the wave moves on.
common_mistakes: Swapping the examples. Sound in air is longitudinal; a wave on a string is transverse.
Writing along the wave without the word parallel — the examiner looks for the direction word.

recall.must_convey: That in a longitudinal wave the particles vibrate parallel to the direction the wave travels.
accept: particles vibrate parallel to the wave direction
vibration is along the line of propagation
reject: vibration is at right angles to the wave

steps.memory_tip: Longitudinal — along. The particle moves along the same line the wave travels on.

insider_note: Both marks live in the two direction words — perpendicular for transverse, parallel for longitudinal — each with one named example.
